content: The antiviral activity of abacavir against HIV-1 has been studied using various laboratory strains and clinical isolates. Against the T-cell tropic strain HIV-1IIIB in lymphoblastic cell lines, the effective concentration to inhibit viral replication by 50% (EC50) ranged from 3.7 to 5.8 μM. For the monocyte/macrophage tropic strain HIV-1BaL in primary monocytes/macrophages, the EC50 ranged from 0.07 to 1.0 μM. Against eight clinical isolates in peripheral blood mononuclear cells, the EC50 was 0.26 ± 0.18 μM. Abacavir demonstrated activity against various HIV-1 clades (A-G) with EC50 values ranging from 0.0015 to 1.05 μM and against HIV-2 isolates with EC50 values between 0.024 and 0.49 μM. Ribavirin at a concentration of 50 μM did not affect the anti-HIV-1 activity of abacavir in cell culture. Lamivudine's antiviral activity against HIV-1 was evaluated in multiple cell lines, including monocytes and fresh human peripheral blood lymphocytes, using standard susceptibility assays. The EC50 values ranged from 0.003 to 15 μM. For therapy-naive individuals with no resistance-associated amino acid substitutions, the median EC50 values were 0.429 μM (range: 0.200 to 2.007 μM) in one study and 2.35 μM (range: 1.37 to 3.68 μM) in another. Lamivudine showed activity against HIV-1 clades (A-G) with EC50 values between 0.001 and 0.120 μM and against HIV-2 isolates with EC50 values from 0.003 to 0.120 μM. However, ribavirin at 50 μM reduced the anti-HIV-1 activity of lamivudine by 3.5-fold in MT-4 cells. The combination of abacavir and lamivudine demonstrated antiviral activity in cell culture against non-subtype B HIV-1 isolates and HIV-2 isolates, with similar efficacy to subtype B isolates. This combination exhibited additive to synergistic effects when used with other antiretroviral agents, including nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs) such as emtricitabine, stavudine, tenofovir, zalcitabine, and zidovudine; non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs) such as delavirdine, efavirenz, and nevirapine; protease inhibitors (PIs) such as amprenavir, indinavir, lopinavir, nelfinavir, ritonavir, and saquinavir; and the fusion inhibitor enfuvirtide. However, ribavirin, when combined with interferon for hepatitis C virus (HCV) treatment, consistently reduced the anti-HIV-1 potency of abacavir/lamivudine by 2to 6-fold in cell culture. HIV-1 isolates with reduced susceptibility to abacavir and lamivudine have been identified in cell culture and in patients failing regimens containing these drugs. Resistance-associated amino acid substitutions in HIV-1 reverse transcriptase (RT) include M184V/I, K65R, L74V, and Y115F. Specifically, the M184V/I substitution, which involves a methionine-to-isoleucine or valine change at codon 184, is a key contributor to lamivudine resistance. In a clinical trial involving therapy-naive adults receiving abacavir (600 mg once daily or 300 mg twice daily) in combination with lamivudine (300 mg) and efavirenz (600 mg), the incidence of virologic failure at 48 weeks was 11% in both dosing groups. Genotypic and phenotypic analyses of virologic failure isolates revealed that the most common resistance-associated substitution was M184V/I, observed in 56% of isolates from the once-daily group and 40% from the twice-daily group. Additionally, 39% of isolates from the once-daily group and 29% from the twice-daily group exhibited a greater than 2.5-fold reduction in abacavir susceptibility. Similarly, 56% of isolates from the once-daily group and 41% from the twice-daily group showed a greater than 2.5-fold reduction in lamivudine susceptibility. Cross-resistance among nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs) has been observed. HIV-1 variants with resistance-associated substitutions, such as K65R, L74V, M184V, and Y115F, exhibit cross-resistance to other NRTIs, including didanosine, emtricitabine, lamivudine, tenofovir, and zalcitabine. The K65R substitution confers resistance to multiple NRTIs, including abacavir, didanosine, emtricitabine, lamivudine, stavudine, tenofovir, and zalcitabine. The L74V substitution is associated with resistance to abacavir, didanosine, and zalcitabine, while the M184V substitution confers resistance to abacavir, didanosine, emtricitabine, lamivudine, and zalcitabine. Viruses with specific combinations of resistance-associated substitutions, such as K65R with or without M184V/I, L74V plus M184V/I, or thymidine analog mutations (TAMs) combined with M184V, demonstrate reduced susceptibility to abacavir/lamivudine. An increasing number of TAMs is associated with a progressive reduction in abacavir susceptibility.
